waypoints.name: Arlberg return option
waypoints.advice: Arlberg return option is where the day begins. Reckon on about 9 °C colder than the valley, and more in the wind. Next is Silvretta High Alpine Road, climbing 239 m.

waypoints.name: Silvretta High Alpine Road
waypoints.advice: You top out at 2032 m here. Reckon on about 10 °C colder than the valley, and more in the wind. Nothing on this route is higher. At this height the road is a summer one: snow gates can stay shut into June and shut again in October. Next is Montafon overnight base, mostly downhill.

waypoints.name: Montafon overnight base
waypoints.advice: 128 km in you reach Montafon overnight base. You lose 1382 m on the way down to it, steadily. Next is Back to Sargans, mostly downhill.

waypoints.name: Back to Sargans
waypoints.advice: Back to Sargans closes the day.

scenicChapters.title: Silvretta High Alpine Road
scenicChapters.narrative: The last of the trees go and the road runs out onto open ground. The summit sits at 2032 m, and what surrounds it is rock, weather and distance — cold comes early up here and stays late. Ride it with something in reserve: the summit is not the end of the work, only the middle of it.
scenicChapters.riderNote: Check the pass is open before you commit to it.

scenicChapters.title: Grand Tour of Switzerland
scenicChapters.narrative: For 83 km this is Grand Tour of Switzerland, a road with a name of its own and a reason for it. Expect company on a summer weekend. Early is better than fast.

silvretta-montafon-overnight-gateway-par.story: Out of St Anton am Arlberg, one way: 192 km, roughly 3 h 39 in the saddle. Silvretta High Alpine Road is the high point. It tops out at 2,032 m. Arlberg Pass and Bielerhohe are subject to seasonal closure - check it is open before you set off. It crosses from Austria into Switzerland - carry ID and check vignette or toll rules. The passes are the reason to go.
